title: per-layer-activation-quant-sensitivity-profiles-feb2025
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the exploratory per-layer activation sensitivity experiments we ran across multiple models and quant strategies (INT8, FP8, AWQ, GPTQ). Goal: build a compact sensitivity map that highlights which layers (weights vs activations) are fragile under activation quantization and which kernels preserve output quality at lowest cost. Intended to guide default quantization configs and kernel selection heuristics in the serving runtime.

Why this differs from previous sweeps:
- Unlike the global-quantization sweeps, this is a per-layer ablation style probe focusing on activation quantization (not only weight-only GPTQ/AWQ).
- We test interaction effects: quantizing single activation layers in isolation, then in small groups (adjacent pairs), to detect non-linear error amplification.
- We include kernel-variant runs (fused attention matmul kernel vs generic GEMM) to see whether certain kernels mask activation quant errors.
- We collect both model-quality deltas (ppl, rouge, instruction-output diffs) and runtime metrics (latency p50/p95, memory delta, throughput).

Scope and models tested:
- Llama-2-7B-chat (base transformer stack)
- MPT-7B-instruct (gated activations variant)
- Falcon-7B (layernorm position differences)
- Small regression checks on Llama-2-13B to validate scale trends (subset of layers)

Quant strategies and kernels:
- AWQ (per-channel weight GPT-style quant for weights) + int8 activations (symmetric, per-tensor scale)
- GPTQ (weight-only) + full-precision activations (baseline)
- FP8 dynamic exponent format for activations (E4M3) with original weight precision
- INT8 activations with different zero-point handling (unsigned vs signed)
- Kernel variants: custom fused-attn kernel v2 (low-precision friendly), reference cuBLAS GEMM path, Triton custom GEMM (experimental)

Hardware/infra:
- Test pods: g5.48xlarge equivalent (A100 80GB) for 7B models; smaller runs on g5.24xlarge (A10G) for sample parity.
- Runtime: branch quant/per-layer-probe (github PR 485) with lightweight instrumentation to flip activation quant for targeted layers at inference time.

Methodology (short):
1) For each model, take a representative evaluation prompt set (1k prompts mixed: math, commonsense, code, dialogue).
2) Run baseline (no activation quant) to capture reference metrics: ppl on heldout, and 3 automatic metrics + 200 sampled human-like scoring prompts for behavioral drift inspection.
3) For each layer i in 0..N-1: enable activation quant only for layer i, keeping weights at baseline precision (or AWQ for weight variants in cross runs). Run inference and record metrics.
4) Repeat for adjacent pairs (i, i+1) and edge groups (first 3 layers, last 3 layers) to capture local amplification.
5) Repeat the above across kernel variants.
6) Aggregate and produce sensitivity score S_i = combination of relative ppl delta, instruction-output edit distance, and failure-rate increase on the sampled correctness prompts.

Key observations (high level):
- Bottleneck layers: For transformer stacks tested, the first 2-4 feedforward blocks (post-embedding) and the last 1-2 decode blocks are most sensitive to activation quantization. S_i for these layers was 3x median.
- Attention softmax outputs appear robust to INT8 activations if the fused-attn kernel is used; however, when using generic GEMM path the same layers show 2x worse quality degradation. Suggests kernel numerics matter a lot for activation quant.
- FP8 activations (E4M3) keep quality within 1% of baseline on most layers but at a 10–15% slower p50 latency vs int8 fused path. Tradeoff: FP8 is attractive where small quality headroom is required.
- AWQ weight quant + int8 activations: the combined error is supra-linear in some mid-stack layers: converting weight+activation in the same layer often causes a larger than expected quality hit. Recommendation: avoid co-quantizing both dims for the top-k sensitive layers.

Representative numbers (Llama-2-7B-chat, 1k prompt eval):
- Baseline ppl: 9.8, baseline p50 latency (single-stream): 120ms
- INT8 activations on layer 3 alone: ppl 10.9 (+11%), p50 118ms (kernel-dependent)
- INT8 activations on layer 24 alone (near top): ppl 12.6 (+29%), p50 122ms
- AWQ weights + no activation quant: ppl 10.2 (+4%)
- AWQ weights + INT8 activations on layer 24: ppl 15.3 (+56%), p50 125ms
- FP8 activations across layer 3: ppl 10.0 (+2%); p50 135ms
- Kernel effect: fused-attn kernel reduced quality delta by ~40% on attention-related layers compared to GEMM path for same INT8 config.

Interpretation / practical heuristics:
- Default quant config: enable AWQ for weights globally, but disable activation INT8 for layers with sensitivity S_i > threshold (we picked threshold=1.8 from normalized S distribution). Those sensitive layers should remain FP32/FP16 activations or use FP8.
- Kernel-aware routing: if runtime chooses an INT8 activation path, prefer nodes with fused-attn kernels available; otherwise downgrade activation quant to FP8 to avoid large quality regressions.
- Batch-aware policies: higher batch sizes partly mask activation quant noise due to better numerical aggregation. For latency-sensitive single-shot requests, be conservative on activation quant in fragile layers.

Detailed run notes (raw-ish):
- Run artifacts saved: s3://redwood-internal/quant-sensitivity/feb2025/ (per-model subfolders). Important artifacts: layer-sensitivity-csvs, raw traces, kernel-numerics logs (reduced mantissa histograms).
- Observed a recurring sign-flip artifact in MPT when quantizing activation pre-gate signals in FFN layer 2: produced repeated token hallucination pattern. Tracked to low dynamic range in that gate path.
- Implementation note: we instrumented per-layer toggles by inserting a dynamic quantization shim that can be toggled via route meta header; this was lightweight and deployed to staging without controller changes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we create a cheap classifier to predict sensitivity S_i from layer statics (activation distribution kurtosis, avg magnitude, layer norm scale) instead of exhaustive per-layer probing? Initial correlation tests show rho~0.55 with activation kurtosis. Worth a small ML model.
- Need to expand to 13B+ models to confirm whether top-layer sensitivity scales linearly with width/depth. We did limited 13B checks but need full sweep.
- Evaluate impact on generation coherence (long-form) — current eval set is mostly short prompts.
- Decide shipping rule for default quant profile for hosted API (e.g., AWQ weights + activation FP8 except for sensitive layer masks) and how to express that in customer config syntax.

Immediate recommendations:
- Ship kernel-detection hook in runtime: allow scheduling policy to prefer fused-attn nodes for any INT8-activation jobs. (INF-3567 ticket created)
- Add per-layer-sensitivity CSVs to model catalog entries; expose a small boolean mask in model metadata that downstream tooling (Optimize) can consume to choose quant profiles.
- For experiments, prefer FP8 fallback on hardware where fused kernels are not available.

Appendix A — experimental matrix snapshot (short):
- Model x {baseline, AWQ-weights, GPTQ-weights} x activation {FP32, FP16, FP8(E4M3), INT8(signed), INT8(unsigned)} x kernel {fused-attn, cuBLAS-GEMM, Triton-GEMM} x layer-ablations {single, adjacent-pair, first3, last3}
- Total runs per model (rough): ~2.4k (we parallelized across 40 pods over 48 hours).

Appendix B — rough script commands and notes to reproduce:
- Branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime:quant/per-layer-probe (PR 485)
- Repro notes: run reproduce.sh --model llama-2-7b --layer 24 --activation int8 --kernel fused-attn --eval-set perf-1k

Notes to self (informal):
- Lina: follow up on MPT gate sign-flip with a targeted small-run to capture pre/post-activation distributions.
- Arjun: add per-layer static feature dump to the artifacts (mean, std, kurtosis, sparsity) — will help the proposed classifier.
- Ethan: start design doc for how Optimize will consume sensitivity masks and surface suggested profiles.

End of doc.
